takeaway: Dry, sunny, and hot again. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) says a mass of dry air over Central America keeps rain odds low all week, with few clouds on the North Pacific today and Nicoya near 35°C. Surf stays offshore every morning through at least Saturday. The new long-period swell is in today, 4–6 ft at 17 seconds, and holds in the 16-second range through Thursday, with the trades getting stronger Thursday night into Friday. October ends dry. The early-November wet spell came back a bit stronger overnight, now centered around Nov 4–6. No tropical threat, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue–Thu, Oct 27–29)
periods.pattern: IMN's Tuesday forecast for the North Pacific is few clouds with occasional gusts in the hills overnight and this morning, then mostly clear this afternoon and tonight. Nicoya's high is about 35°C with a low near 22°C, and Liberia reaches about 35°C. IMN says the country stays very stable this week because of dry air over Central America and the Caribbean. Any showers stay in the mountains of the South Pacific and southern Caribbean. Every model keeps Nosara at 1–3 mm a day or less.
periods.implications: Great days for anything outdoors. It gets hot by late morning, so plan the beach and errands early, and bring water.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri Oct 30 – Mon Nov 2)
periods.pattern: The northeast-to-east breeze keeps blowing across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica in every model. Nosara stays near dry, 1–3 mm a day, through Sunday. On Monday the American average shows up to about 9 mm (a third of an inch), the European averages only 2–4 mm. The regular European run shows a weak, shallow low just off Nicoya around Saturday evening, but it brings almost no rain here.
periods.implications: Mostly dry, sunny, and breezy through the weekend. A passing evening shower becomes possible by Monday, nothing that should wreck plans.
periods.confidence: High through Sunday, moderate for Monday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Tue Nov 3 – Tue Nov 10)
periods.pattern: The band of tropical showers that has sat south of Costa Rica drifts north over the Nicoya coast. Near Nosara, the model averages show about 6–9 mm a day on Nov 3, then a peak around Nov 4 of roughly 16–29 mm (0.6–1.1 inch) in the day, up from 9–16 mm in yesterday's run. Amounts ease to about 9–16 mm on Nov 6 and drop to a few millimeters a day by Nov 8–10. The regular European run, dry in yesterday's version, now shows about 16 mm on Nov 3 and about 35 mm (1.4 inch) on Nov 5. The trades still blow over Nicaragua, but they go lighter near Nosara around Nov 4–6. IMN's long-range outlook still calls for drier than normal on the Pacific side through Nov 22, with the dry season settling in on the North Pacific.
periods.implications: Keep Nov 3–6 a little flexible. A couple of showery afternoons or evenings look more likely than they did yesterday, possibly with a heavier downpour. It still doesn't look like a multi-day soaking.
periods.confidence: High on a dry end to October. Moderate that early November turns showery, low on how much rain falls.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, so it's offshore at Nosara every morning through at least Saturday. Winds are light to moderate today through Thursday, then stronger from Thursday night into Friday.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:44 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast winds of 10–15 knots today, with 4–6 ft of west swell at 17 seconds. Tonight it's northeast 10 knots, 15–20 knots out in the Gulf of Papagayo, with south-southwest swell at 17 seconds. Wednesday is northeast 10–15 with 3–5 ft at 16 seconds. Thursday turns northeast to east 10–15 with 4–6 ft at 16 seconds. Friday is the windiest, northeast to east 20 knots in the gulf and 10–15 elsewhere, with 4–6 ft at 14 seconds, and Saturday stays northeast to east 10–15 with 4–6 ft at 15–16 seconds. One caution: the waters just south of the peninsula have a west-northwest wind turning northeast this afternoon, southeast breezes Wednesday and Thursday, and scattered showers and storms. Nosara sits near that edge, so afternoons could go side-on sooner than further north. Nicaragua looks offshore all day through the weekend, a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but Nosara won't necessarily stay offshore all day. Around Nov 4–6 the models weaken the trades near Nosara, which would bring more onshore afternoons.
surfWinds.bestWindows: This morning through Thursday morning for the 16–17-second swell in light offshore wind. Long-period sets come bigger and less often than the average height suggests, and rip currents get stronger. Friday and Saturday mornings bring southwest swell at 14–16 seconds in firmer offshore wind, so early is cleanest and the afternoon may get a little bumpy.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings through Saturday. Moderate on how long afternoons hold. Low to moderate for the Nov 4–6 stretch.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, still low, but slightly higher than yesterday. Nothing is building in the next week.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: If anything comes, it's around Nov 3–6.
gyreWatch.supporting: All the model averages bring the shower band south of Costa Rica north over Nicoya in early November, and today's runs are wetter than yesterday's, peaking around Nov 4. The regular European run now agrees, with a wet Nov 5 and weak shallow lows off Nicoya on Oct 31 and southwest of Costa Rica on Nov 2.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model shows a broad, slow-spinning low parked off Costa Rica, and the trades keep blowing over Nicaragua, which works against a soaking setup. The wet signal is only a few days long and fades by Nov 8. IMN expects dry conditions on the Pacific side for Nov 2–8 and drier than normal through Nov 22, with low odds (about 10%) of an extreme event. The U.S. hurricane center expects no new storms in the East Pacific or the Caribbean in the next week. Tropical Storm Vance is far away, southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico.

whatChanged: The early-November wet signal came back stronger: the model averages now peak around Nov 4 at roughly 16–29 mm, up from 9–16 mm, and the regular European run went from mostly dry to wet on Nov 3–5. The offshore pattern now runs through Saturday, and Friday's trades look stronger than yesterday's call. The long-period swell arrived on schedule today at 17 seconds. IMN's weekly and long-range outlooks are unchanged, and there are no new IMN notices since Sunday's for the Central and South Pacific.
practical: Surf early each morning this week while the long-period swell runs in light offshore wind, and watch for stronger rip currents. Friday and Saturday mornings are still offshore, just windier. The week stays sunny, hot, and dry, so it's a good stretch for outdoor plans. Keep Nov 3–6 flexible for a few showery afternoons or evenings. There's no tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
